fullDesc: On January 1, 1863 President Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation, declaring enslaved people in Confederate-held areas to be free. It changed the aims of the Civil War and allowed Black men to join the Union army.
realFacts: About 180,000 Black men served in the Union army
It did not free enslaved people in the border states
The 13th Amendment ended slavery in December 1865
Freedom came as Union troops advanced
